action.title: Select the end-to-end dataflow family

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: A800 tensor cores strongly favor BF16 matrix tiles with FP32 accumulation; H=2048 and expected triple_hidden=6144 are well aligned, while the depthwise width-4 convolution is too small to dominate arithmetic.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Retaining two large vendor GEMMs maps well to A800 tensor cores and produced a measured 1.53x mean speedup.

memory_bandwidth.notes: The measured packed-staged implementation eliminates transpose, padding, Bx, and conv_out materialization, although packed BCx and y remain global intermediates.

register_pressure.notes: The successful fused pointwise-depthwise stage uses bounded 8x64 tiles; more aggressive fusion could increase occupancy risk.

nodes.notes: Measured evidence now favors staged mappings that preserve regular tensor-core GEMMs while fusing the low-arithmetic-intensity causal-convolution region. The packed-staged family is the incumbent at 0.6332403 ms versus 0.9749163 ms reference.

action.description: Implement the packed 3H projection, a fused gate-plus-causal-convolution-plus-C-gate stage that emits contiguous y, and a separate final projection.
action.rationale: This preserves large, regular tensor-core GEMMs while removing transpose, padding, Bx, and conv_out materialization. It is the lowest-risk first performance implementation.
action.title: Prototype packed-projection staged dataflow

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: The [BT,2048]x[2048,6144] and [BT,2048]x[2048,2048] operations match A800 BF16 tensor-core shapes cleanly.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: The two dominant BF16 projections remain on highly optimized GEMM paths, fitting A800 tensor-core hardware well.

memory_bandwidth.notes: The staged BCx and gated-y tensors add global traffic, but contiguous packed projections and vendor GEMMs provide strong realized throughput.

register_pressure.notes: The custom stage keeps only a small time-by-channel tile and four causal accumulations live; all five workloads passed.

nodes.notes:
CURRENT:
- does: Materializes the packed triple projection with F.linear, processes its B/C/x_proj slices in a Triton gate-convolution kernel, and finishes with a second F.linear.
- bottleneck: compute, primarily the two dense GEMMs, with secondary intermediate-memory traffic.
FOLLOW_THROUGH:
- aligned_with_intent: yes
UPDATE_BELIEF:
- The family passed all five workloads at about 1.53x reference speed, strongly validating staged packed projection as the best currently measured end-to-end mapping.
- next bet: Preserve the GEMM-based structure and pursue low-risk launch and tile specialization in the middle kernel, since replacing the family would incur substantially greater implementation risk.

action.description: Implement one projection path that directly emits B*x_proj, a second path for C, then fuse C with the causal convolution before the standalone output projection.
action.rationale: Partitioning the three projections can avoid writing and rereading separate B and x_proj tensors, reducing intermediate footprint while retaining a regular final GEMM.
action.title: Prototype projection-partitioned staged dataflow

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: The B/x_proj producer has two H-wide output groups sharing the same K reduction, while C is another H-wide projection; all dimensions remain tensor-core aligned on A800.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: The family delegates dense 2048-wide reductions to highly tuned GEMMs and uses Triton only for the elementwise depthwise stencil, matching A800 hardware well.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Materializing projected and gated intermediates costs bandwidth, but packed projection layout and causal time reuse make the staged family consistently fast.

register_pressure.notes: Partitioning the two GEMMs from the stencil avoids attempting to retain hidden-dimension reduction state and causal state in one oversized kernel.

nodes.notes: The successful TIME_TILE=4 descendant raises confidence in projection-partitioned staging: all five workloads passed at 0.6230297 ms and 1.559x reference speed. Further work should refine the causal time axis without disturbing the two efficient GEMM stages.

action.description: Implement a small-BT specialized kernel that computes projected channel tiles for the required causal rows and immediately accumulates their gated values into an output-projection tile.
action.rationale: For very few tokens, eliminating launches and all large activation intermediates may outweigh duplicated projection work and lower occupancy.
action.title: Prototype end-to-end output-tile dataflow

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: H=2048 is aligned, but each output-column tile needs all H gated channels; without cross-program communication, producing those channels can repeat the first projection for multiple output tiles.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: The plan trades activation traffic and launch overhead for a more complex nested reduction. It is plausible only when BT is too small to amortize staged execution.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Projection recomputation across output tiles can multiply the dominant FLOPs and overwhelm any fusion benefit.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Avoids writing BCx, Bx, C, conv_out, and y; only inputs, weights, biases, and final output need global-memory traffic.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Large projection weights may be reread by many programs, making effective weight bandwidth worse than staged GEMMs.

register_pressure.notes: Output accumulators coexist with B/C/x_proj values for current and halo tokens plus convolution state.
register_pressure.risk: High pressure can cause spills or force output tiles so narrow that first-projection work is heavily duplicated.

nodes.notes:
Intended regime: very small BT and especially tiny sequence lengths. Tiling philosophy: own an output tile and stream hidden-channel contributions through the causal middle expression. Memory strategy: keep projected fragments and four-tap state on chip and write only final output. Strength: minimum activation traffic and launch count. Weakness: difficult mapping, changed rounding boundaries, and likely duplicated first-projection work. Primary limiter: redundant compute and register capacity.
SELF_CHECK: This is mutually exclusive with both staged siblings because it removes the BCx/Bx/C/y interfaces and assigns projection production to final-output tiles.

action.title: Shape-specialize the fused gate and causal-convolution stage

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: The schedule is well matched to A800: tensor-core GEMMs handle dense work and the fused pointwise/depthwise stage uses larger tiles and more warps only where sequence length supports them.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Shape specialization improves coalescing and limits inactive lanes, although overlapping causal windows still cause repeated packed-projection loads.

register_pressure.notes: The tested tile schedule balances occupancy and live state across the observed sequence regimes and passed every correctness workload.

action.description: Replace the one-row-per-program convolution kernel with a small time-by-channel tile. Load each B and x_proj value in the causal halo once, compute multiple adjacent convolution outputs, apply their corresponding C gates, and preserve the existing packed input and regular output GEMMs.
action.rationale: The current kernel reloads most B and x_proj elements for four neighboring output rows. A time tile can reduce these reads toward one per halo element while keeping the proven staged dataflow and numerical order.

register_pressure.notes: The four-output implementation has a moderate live-value set and remains a safer occupancy point than larger time tiles.

action.title: Test a 128-channel block for the eight-warp tile-eight kernel

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Eight warps over 128 channels provide only 16 channels per warp, which likely underutilizes vector work and increases instruction and launch overhead relative to the prior wider block.

memory_bandwidth.notes: The 128-channel block increases program count and repeats fixed per-program work. Although it may improve occupancy, the measured aggregate latency indicates that the extra scheduling and memory traffic were not recovered.

register_pressure.notes: Halving the channel block reduces registers held per program and is structurally safer for the unrolled tile-eight and tile-sixteen paths, but this register relief did not translate into a net speedup.

nodes.notes:
CURRENT:

For sequence lengths at least 128 it assigns eight warps and a 128-channel block before the final PyTorch output projection.
- bottleneck: latency and scheduling overhead, with a secondary memory-bandwidth cost from the increased number of channel programs.
FOLLOW_THROUGH:
- aligned_with_intent: yes. The tile-eight path uses the intended 128-channel block with eight warps, although the implementation also applies that block size to the tile-sixteen path.
UPDATE_BELIEF:
- The implementation passed all 5 workloads, confirming numerical safety, but latency was 0.6432561 ms versus the 0.6245817 ms prior trace and approximately 0.623 ms best ancestor. Register relief from block 128 is therefore outweighed by extra program and warp overhead in the aggregate workload.
- next bet: Confine block 128 to the intended tile-eight regime and restore block 256 for tile sixteen. This isolates whether applying the refinement to the more heavily unrolled long-sequence path caused the regression.
PERF_GAP:
- expected_vs_baseline_factor: 0.636 latency ratio.
- observed_vs_baseline_factor: 0.660 latency ratio (0.6432561 / 0.9749163), about 3.8% slower than predicted.
- hypothesized_reason: Eight warps over only 128 channels expose too little work per warp, and applying the same narrow block to TIME_TILE=16 increases program-count overhead enough to erase the expected occupancy benefit.

register_pressure.notes: TIME_TILE=16 keeps a large projection halo and many convolution accumulators live; BLOCK_SIZE=256 with eight warps can constrain occupancy.

kernel_summary: This is a mixed two-GEMM plus fixed-width causal depthwise-stencil workload with dense BF16 inputs and outputs: a [BT,2048] to [BT,3H] projection dominates arithmetic, the B*x_proj gate and four-tap convolution introduce local dependence on the previous three sequence positions, and a [BT,2048] output projection supplies the remaining dense reduction. On A800, the main objective is to preserve tensor-core efficiency for H=2048 while eliminating transpose, padding, and temporary middle-stage traffic; packed staging is the safest general design, partitioned projection may reduce large-BT bandwidth, and end-to-end fusion is credible only for very small BT because it risks projection recomputation and excessive register state. Correctness depends on triple_hidden being exactly 6144, causal zero padding, weight orientation, and acceptable changes to BF16 rounding boundaries.
open_questions: Is triple_hidden guaranteed to equal exactly 3*hidden_size=6144 for every invocation, as required by chunk(3) and the subsequent grouped convolution?
What concrete batch_size and seq_len distributions define the typical workload, and should dispatch specialize separately for very small, moderate, and large batch_size*seq_len?
Are all input tensors guaranteed contiguous with the exact strides implied by their listed shapes, or must arbitrary PyTorch strides be supported?
What implementation constitutes the measured baseline: the eager reference sequence, torch.compile, cuBLAS/cuDNN, or an existing Triton kernel?
Must the fused implementation preserve BF16 materialization and rounding after F.linear, elementwise products, convolution, and y, or is any result within the stated tolerance accepted?
Are zero-length sequences, seq_len below four, unusual bias dtypes, or aliased input/output storage part of the correctness domain?
May the solution dispatch among multiple Triton kernels and shape-specialized paths, or is a single launch or single kernel required?
